Estimate temporal, contemporaneous and between-person networks from panel data

Source: R/panelgvar.R
panel_gvar.Rd

panel_gvar() estimates temporal, contemporaneous and between-person networks from panel data, which follow many persons over a few measurement waves. It fits the panel graphical vector-autoregressive (panel-GVAR) model, which separates three kinds of association among the measured variables (Epskamp, 2020).

The temporal network is directed: an edge from A to B is the within-person effect of A at one wave on B at the next, given all other variables, and a self-loop is an autoregressive effect. The contemporaneous network holds the partial correlations among a person's deviations at the same wave that the temporal effects leave unexplained. The between network holds the partial correlations among the persons' stable means. Together they distinguish variables that predict one another over time within persons, that vary together within persons at the same wave, and that differ together between persons.

The model is fitted by maximum likelihood to long data (one row per person and wave) or wide data (one row per person). By default every edge is estimated and reported with its standard error, p-value, 95% Wald interval and a significant flag at alpha. select = "prune" removes the edges that are not significant and refits the model, then adds back removed edges that improve the fit (stepup). select = "ebic" estimates the three networks with a lasso penalty chosen by the extended Bayesian information criterion (EBIC), the panel counterpart of ebic_glasso(). The fitted model is checked against its optimality conditions (see Details), and as.data.frame(x, what = "diagnostics") reports the result.

The result is a psychnet_panelgvar object holding the three networks (psychnet_panelgvar).

The model needs at least three waves. For a network from cross-sectional data, use psychnet(); for networks of within-person deviations without a temporal model, psychnet() with within. The model is the one fitted by psychonetrics::panelgvar().

Usage

panel_gvar(
  data,
  vars,
  id = NULL,
  wave = NULL,
  select = c("none", "prune", "ebic"),
  alpha = 0.01,
  adjust = "none",
  recursive = FALSE,
  stepup = TRUE,
  criterion = c("bic", "none"),
  gamma = 0.5,
  nlambda = 50L,
  lambda_min_ratio = 1e-04,
  refit = FALSE,
  standardize = c("none", "z", "z_per_wave"),
  labels = NULL,
  na_method = "listwise"
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or matrix: long (one row per person per wave; give vars, id and wave) or wide (one row per person; give vars as a design matrix).

vars

Long data: the names of the variable columns. Wide data: a character matrix of column names with one row per variable and one column per wave (the psychonetrics design); its row names become the labels.

id, wave

Long data only: the names of the person and wave columns. Neither may contain missing values or be one of vars, and each person has at most one row per wave. Waves are ordered by factor level order, by value for numbers, dates and times, numerically for character values that are all numbers, and alphabetically (with a warning) for any other character values; pass a factor to set the order.

select

Edge selection: "none" (default) estimates every edge and reports its significance; "prune" removes non-significant edges and refits (see Details); "ebic" estimates penalized networks with the penalty chosen by EBIC.

alpha

Significance level, in (0, 1), for the significant flag, the solid and dashed edges of plot(), and pruning. Default 0.01, as in psychonetrics::prune().

adjust

Multiplicity correction for the p-values tested in pruning, one of stats::p.adjust.methods. Default "none". Used only with select = "prune"; the reported p-values and significant flags are always unadjusted.

recursive

With select = "prune": repeat pruning until no edge has p > alpha. Default FALSE.

stepup

With select = "prune": after pruning, add back removed edges that improve the fit (see Details). Default TRUE, because one-pass pruning can remove parameters that are each non-significant but jointly significant, such as an autoregression and correlated cross-lagged effects. FALSE gives pruning alone.

criterion

With stepup: "bic" (default) also requires BIC to decrease when an edge is added; "none" uses the significance tests only.

gamma, nlambda, lambda_min_ratio

With select = "ebic": the EBIC hyperparameter (default 0.5), the number of penalty values (default 50, a whole number >= 2), and the smallest penalty as a fraction of the largest (default 1e-4).

refit

With select = "ebic": refit the selected networks by unpenalized maximum likelihood, so that standard errors and p-values are available. Default FALSE returns the penalized estimates, for which standard errors, p-values and significant are NA.

standardize

Rescaling before fitting: "none" (default), "z" (one mean and standard deviation per variable, pooled over waves), or "z_per_wave" (each variable z-scored within each wave). "z_per_wave" removes changes in means and variances across waves, which the model would otherwise assume absent, and makes the edges standardized. Standardization uses the available values before listwise deletion.

labels

Optional node labels, unique and non-empty (default: vars for long data, the design row names for wide data).

na_method

Only "listwise" (default): a person with any missing value is dropped. "pairwise" is refused, because a pairwise covariance is not a likelihood for this model.

Value

An object of class c("psychnet_panelgvar", "netobject_group") (psychnet_panelgvar): a named list of three networks of class psychnet, temporal (directed), contemporaneous and between (undirected). as.data.frame() gives one row per edge with its standard error, p-value and Wald interval; as.data.frame(x, what = ...) gives the "parameters", "fit" indices, "variance" decomposition, "covariance" matrices, EBIC "path" or "diagnostics", whose score column is the certificate. summary() gives one row per network and plot() draws the three networks.

Details

Write \(y_{it}\) for the scores of person \(i\) at wave \(t\). The model is \(y_{it} = \mu + b_i + w_{it}\), with means \(\mu\) shared by all waves, stable person deviations \(b_i\) with covariance \(\Sigma_b\), and a stationary within-person process \(w_{it} = B w_{i,t-1} + \zeta_{it}\) with innovation covariance \(\Sigma_\zeta\). The temporal network is \(B\) (the edge from \(j\) to \(i\) is \(B_{ij}\)); the contemporaneous and between networks are the partial correlations implied by \(\Sigma_\zeta\) and \(\Sigma_b\). When the means drift across waves, standardize = "z_per_wave" removes the drift.

Pruning fixes to zero, in one pass, every temporal, contemporaneous and between edge whose Wald p-value (after adjust) exceeds alpha, and refits; recursive = TRUE repeats until every remaining edge is significant. The step-up search then frees the removed edge with the largest modification index while that index is significant at alpha, and keeps it when the likelihood-ratio test of the refit is significant at alpha and, with criterion = "bic", BIC decreases; the first rejected edge ends the search. This is psychonetrics' prune() followed by stepup().

With select = "ebic", the lasso penalty applies to the temporal (autoregressive effects included), contemporaneous and between parameters on the data scale, over nlambda log-spaced values from the smallest penalty that empties every network down to lambda_min_ratio times that value. The selected penalty minimizes \(\mathrm{EBIC} = -2 \log L + k \log n + 4 \gamma k \log V\), with \(k\) the number of nonzero free parameters, \(n\) the number of persons and \(V\) the number of wave-by-variable columns. Penalized estimates below 1e-5 in absolute value on the data scale are set to zero before the certificate is computed.

The certificate is the largest absolute gradient of the likelihood over the free parameters or, for select = "ebic" without refit, the largest violation of the lasso optimality (Karush–Kuhn–Tucker) conditions. Pruned and penalized models are refitted or re-solved after selection, so the certificate refers to the networks returned. It is computed on standardized variables and does not depend on the variables' units. The likelihood is not convex: a value near zero shows a stationary point, and the fit is started from several points whose agreement is reported.

Conditions

psychnet_bad_input when data, vars, id or wave cannot be resolved (columns missing or duplicated, id and wave the same or among vars, missing persons or waves, a person with two rows in one wave), a variable is not numeric, there are fewer than two variables or fewer than three waves, there are no more complete persons than wave-by-variable columns, the stacked covariance is singular, a variable does not vary as standardize requires, labels is invalid, an argument is outside its allowed values, or na_method is not "listwise"; psychnet_no_converge (error) when no start reaches a feasible optimum, the fitted model is worse than its nested baseline, or no penalized model is feasible. Warnings: psychnet_no_converge when the score exceeds 1e-6 at an interior solution; psychnet_boundary when the contemporaneous or between covariance is near singular (partial correlations near +/-1, common with three waves), so estimates involving it are unreliable; psychnet_singular_information when some parameters are not identified at the estimate (their standard errors are NA); psychnet_approximate_se when a fit being pruned had a singular information and its unidentified parameters were pruned; psychnet_listwise_drop when persons are removed for missing values; psychnet_wave_order when character waves are ordered alphabetically; psychnet_ignored_argument when adjust is set without pruning.

References

Epskamp, S. (2020). Psychometric network models from time-series and panel data. Psychometrika, 85(1), 206-231. doi:10.1007/s11336-020-09697-3

Foygel, R., & Drton, M. (2010). Extended Bayesian information criteria for Gaussian graphical models. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 23, 604-612.

See also

psychnet_panelgvar for reading the fit; ebic_glasso() for cross-sectional data; psychnet() with within; certificate() for the certificates of the other estimators.

Examples

# srl_panel: 100 students x 4 weeks, simulated from a panel-GVAR in which
# effort in one week drives efficacy in the next.
fit <- panel_gvar(srl_panel,
                  vars = c("efficacy", "planning", "effort", "enjoyment",
                           "anxiety"),
                  id = "student", wave = "week")
fit
#> <psychnet_panelgvar> panel graphical VAR (temporal + contemporaneous + between)
#>   persons: 100   waves: 4   nodes: 5
#>   edges (significant/estimated, p < 0.01): temporal 1/20 (+4/5 autoregressive)   contemporaneous 5/10   between 2/10
#>   selection: none (full model)
#>   fit: chisq(170) = 207.19, p = 0.0273   CFI = 0.957   TLI = 0.946   RMSEA = 0.047
#>   optimality (ML score): 8.16e-13
#>   starts: 3 of 3 reached the best saturated optimum
